verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y — X wins narrowly. Both find the same 7 execution sites with correct traces, and both are strong on mechanism. The separating material is verified and specific: X reports FOUR stale cross-file citations (ship-land's "deploy-live.sh:2543 dies DIVERGED" vs the real block at :2467/die at :2472/:2601; plist:16 → operator-readout.sh:238-246 vs :517-518; cc-do:152's "§152-258" vs :503-546; deploy-live.sh:185 calling deploy-now "deploy-live.sh --force" when :89 forwards only "$@") — I opened all four and all four hold, and the brief explicitly demands this verification. Y reports none, and worse, Y's answer to (c) is grounded ON a comment ("corroborated in-scope by scripts/deploy-now.sh:69-70's own comment"), which is the precise practice the brief forbids, and yields the flat false claim that the only unattended entry point is outside the scoped trees. X also adjudicates two further generic dispatchers Y never touches (cc-backlog:4308's `falsify` argv probe; cc-premise:1776 filing_day_screen, which returns UNDECIDABLE on a script call at :1791-1794 rather than running it) and the second run_one call site at cc-do:497, and traces cc-do's execution dispatch (:525/:535-541/:543-548) that Y explicitly says it did not read. Against that, X has three off-by-one citations (cc-do:358 for the line at :359 — the key's S5 and the hardest site; cc-do:357 for the :358 CONFIRM arm; operator-readout:533 for the :532 gate) and a non-reproducible grep self-report (273 vs the actual 316). Those are precision defects on sites X identifies and quotes verbatim correctly; the material X adds that Y lacks is new verified content. X, narrowly.

X vs Z — tie. Each has exactly one deliverable-level defect and each holds material the other lacks. X gets the 7th execution site (cc-do:454) with a fully verified producer trace: deploy-live.sh:708/:728/:731/:734/:743/:746 build `run=` strings naming deploy-live.sh, :812 stores them via `cc-backlog needs --run`, cc-do:415 reads `.run`, cc-do:454 runs it. Z rejects that site on a claim I verified FALSE — "None of the non-comment deploy-live lines in scope passes it as a --run argument" — and never mentions :812 at all, which is why Z lands on 6 instead of 7. Conversely Z has zero bad citations against X's three (including the cc-do:359 site line), the most complete near-miss list of the three (uniquely covering operator-readout:541, cc-do:194/:196-198, deploy-live.sh:419/:1483/:2471, permission-gate-lint:104, offbox-admission-lint:274, ship-land:4511, host-suites.manifest — all of which I opened and all of which match their stated reasons), and several unique verified mechanism facts X lacks: --falsify-host always exits within :339-408 before the arg loop at :411; cc-premise's seams at :129/:241/:246; the upstream cc-backlog claim path at :3046/:2480/:3579 with an explicit scope disclosure; deploy-now.sh:62 and :83-87. One site missed on a false premise versus three wrong line numbers plus a thinner (b): neither difference dominates.

Y vs Z — Z wins. Y's one advantage is real: it counts cc-do:454 as a site with a correct producer trace, where Z's rejection premise is verifiably false. But Z has three specific, verified, material advantages against it. (1) Z verified and reported three stale cross-file citations with line numbers (ship-land.sh:1703, plist:16, cc-do:152) and additionally named one citation it deliberately did not rely on; Y reports none and instead leans on deploy-now.sh:69-70's comment as evidence for a cross-file fact, producing the flat false exclusivity claim in (c). (2) Z's part (b) is materially more complete against a brief that asks for EVERY rejected near-miss — I opened roughly a dozen of Z's unique rows and every one matched. (3) Z read cc-do's execution dispatch (:525, :535-540, :543-548) that Y states it did not read, so Y's site 3 is incompletely grounded on the "when does it run" axis the brief asks for. Three verified advantages against one.
